title: Elastic Fleet Transition Policy — non-disruptive GPU slice reshuffle
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and implement an Elastic Fleet Transition Policy that enables rolling software/firmware changes across dedicated GPU slices with minimal SLA impact. This ticket introduces a 'reshuffle' primitive: a controlled, reversible GPU-slice migration which cooperates with the autoscaler and tenant admission windows to avoid token surges and packet loss during upgrades. Unlike prior drain-first approaches, reshuffle emphasizes transient islanding and soft-eviction to preserve throughput for high-QoS tenants.
acceptance_criteria: New transition API implemented in fleet-controller allowing 'reshape' and 'soft-evict' modes
Autoscaler handshake implemented so scale-up operations defer until slice handoffs complete
End-to-end upgrade run (staging) demonstrates <5% p99 latency drift and <2% throughput loss for affected tenants
Rollout gates support per-tenant admission windows and emergency rollback triggers
Runbook and playbook published in Confluence with sign-off from SRE and Platform PM
implementation_notes:
Architecture:
- Introduce FleetTransition CRD with phases: prepare -> isolate -> reshape -> validate -> commit -> release.
- Prepare: mark target slice read-only for new long-running sessions and notify autoscaler. Create short lease tokens that let existing KV caches persist for N minutes.
- Isolate: apply network priority shaping to drain queued requests off the slice gradually (soft-evict). Do not evict in-flight inference; prefer migration to sibling slices when possible.
- Reshape: apply upgrade (kernel/driver/model artifact) inside a canary container while a mirrored traffic shadow validates outputs.
- Validate: run synthetic and sampled real-request checks against baselines, check model outputs for regressions using prompt-set eval harness.
- Commit: switch routing, release lease tokens, update routing table and analytics counters.
- Release: inform autoscaler to rebalance if needed.

Autoscaler handoff:
- New handoff API: fleet-controller.reserveCapacity(slice_id, duration) -> returns hold token.
- Autoscaler must accept hold token and delay scale-to-zero/scale-in until hold expires or is explicitly released.

Trade-offs and choices:
- Soft-evict increases tail latency risk for a short period but avoids large cold-start spikes when evicting many tenants simultaneously.
- Mirror-validation adds cost but is required for safety on model/driver changes.

Telemetry:
- Emit transition.start/finish events, per-tenant latency/throughput deltas, and hold-token usage. Track cumulative capacity hedged during rollout.
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (Canary): 2 slices in staging region. Run shadow validation for 6 hours; monitor p50/p90/p99 and model-output diffs.
Stage 1 (Small wave): 5% of customer-facing slices; enable per-tenant admission windows and run a single rolling reshuffle per hour.
Stage 2 (Regional): 20% of slices in region with conservative autoscaler holds and extended validation.
Stage 3 (Global): full rollout with dynamic pacing informed by monitored regression metrics and capacity hedging.
Rollback: immediate cancel on automated regression alert or manual stop: reshape is reversible by reapplying previous image and rebalancing routes; autoscaler holds remain until manual release.
test_plan: Unit tests for FleetTransition CRD state machine and hold-token lifecycle
Integration test: simulated multi-tenant cluster with fake autoscaler exercising hold and release flows
Staging run: 48-hour canary with real traffic shaping against production-like dataset (use traffic replay harness)
Chaos test: randomly kill control-plane replicas during reshape to ensure idempotence and safe retries
Load test: verify autoscaler does not scale in below reserved capacity while holds active
risks: If lease duration is mis-sized, long-running sessions may hold capacity for too long leading to wasted GPUs
Shadow validation may produce false positives for nondeterministic models; need robust diff thresholds
Autoscaler cooperation is required; partial rollout without autoscaler changes could cause capacity thrash
Metric gaps: missing per-tenant KV cache eviction metrics could hide regressions during reshape

2026-02-27 Architecture review: consensus to prefer soft-evict over full drain for first pass. Concern raised by SRE about lease token leakage — added TTL enforcement.

2026-03-05 Perf run results: reshuffle in staging (2 slices) showed 4.1% p99 drift for one tenant due to KV cache coldness; reduced TTL from 15m to 8m for subsequent runs.

notes: Follow-up work: metricizing per-tenant cache warmup time (separate ticket), and exploring an adaptive TTL that shrinks for low-impact tenants. Consider exposing a customer-facing 'upgrade-safe window' API for enterprise customers to opt into quieter upgrade windows.
